name: Zencal
tagline: Publish booking pages and collect optional payments through a simple workflow

pricing.notes: Typical Pro monthly equivalent; vendor billing may be in EUR.

tiers.name: Light
tiers.limits: Maximum 1 user; unlimited meetings, topics, and calendars.
tiers.notes: Annual plan gives 2 months free; Clients module is +$10/month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited meetings, topics, and calendars; 1 user included.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Up to 20 users; unlimited meetings, topics, and calendars.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); 14-day trial; Enterprise custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Optional modules are separately priced: Events +$10/month, Bundles +$10, Analytics +$10, Clients +$10, Client Portal +$28, Conversions +$8; SMS costs $0.08 each outside Enterprise; displayed prices are gross.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Zencal, publish booking pages and collect optional payments through a simple workflow. The hard boundary is calendar connections, payments, reminders, team access, and hosted reliability, plus calendar integrations and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Read one calendar, publish booking pages with availability, collect optional payments, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
whatYouLose: calendar connections, payments, reminders, team access, and hosted reliability
ongoingBurden: OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Zencal because people pay because one double booking or missed invite can cost more than years of subscription fees. The recurring cost buys OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cal.com
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source scheduling platform with calendar integrations and booking workflows.

alternatives.name: Cal.com Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited solo event types, calendars and bookings, with payments and notifications; team routing costs money.

facts.dataFormat: Account, availability, booking and integration records live in Cal.com's cloud and in the connected calendar, conferencing and payment providers
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan is built for one person, while team routing and shared scheduling cost extra and the workflow is less payment-service-focused than Zencal.

alternatives.name: TidyCal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited one-person booking types and paid bookings on one calendar; group meetings and fancy emails cost extra.

facts.dataFormat: Account, connected-calendar, appointment and payment-integration records live in TidyCal and AppSumo's cloud services
facts.gapVsPaid: It connects one calendar and omits custom intake questions, reminders and group bookings on the free plan.

alternatives.name: YouCanBookMe Free
alternatives.desc: One booking page, but it keeps forms, payments, confirmations, polls and the calendar-overlay trick.

facts.install: Hosted signup followed by connecting a supported calendar
facts.dataFormat: Booking and account records live in YouCanBookMe's cloud, while availability is read from and events are written to the connected Google, Microsoft or Apple calendar
facts.gapVsPaid: It is limited to one booking page and one calendar, retains branding and requires a connected external calendar.
facts.setupBlocker: A supported external calendar must be connected before a booking page can work

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited links and calendars, custom questions, email reminders and Stripe payments; teams are paid and zcal takes 3%.

facts.dataFormat: Account and booking records live in zcal's cloud; Stripe processes and stores payment details for paid bookings
facts.gapVsPaid: Stripe payments carry a 3% commission and teams are paid, with less service-client workflow depth than Zencal.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a single-user booking service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Zencal in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Google Calendar OAuth, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: read one calendar, publish booking pages with availability, collect optional payments, create conflict-safe bookings, and send confirmations and reminders.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one account with configurable working hours, buffers, minimum notice, and booking horizon.
Connect Google Calendar using OAuth and store refresh tokens encrypted at rest.
Calculate availability in UTC and render it in the visitor's detected timezone.
Reserve slots transactionally, create calendar events, and prevent concurrent double booking.
Send confirmation, cancellation, and reminder email with signed management links.
Add an admin booking list, event-type editor, audit log, and calendar reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out Microsoft and Apple calendar support.
Deliberately leave out team round-robin routing.
Deliberately leave out payments, CRM workflows, and enterprise controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
